correction: Enforce the original spawnSync aggregate 65536-byte stdout/stderr ceiling, rather than two independent pipe ceilings. Retain the fixed system executable, stdin-only secret transport, generic errors and production 15-second deadline.

tests.deadline_clock: Tokio paused clock with real OS children; exact production timer, not mock runner outputs
tests.awaited_timeout_and_overflow_cleanup: direct owned child already reaped before error returned; waitpid(WNOHANG)==ECHILD, kill(pid,0)==ESRCH
tests.cancellation_cleanup: drop is nonblocking; eventual direct child kill/reap while runtime remains live, without advancing the paused 15-second clock

primary_source.behavior: SyncProcessStdioPipe::OnRead charges all output pipes through the same buffered_output_size_ counter; overflow occurs when aggregate captured bytes exceed max_buffer_.

scope_limits: Production spawning remains hardcoded to /usr/bin/security; the executable selection seam is private and tests only invoke owned /bin/sh builtins, with private FIFO gates and no descendants.

The 15-second body covers stdin writes and closure, both output pipes and child wait. The clock assertions use the actual production duration under a paused Tokio clock, not 15 seconds of elapsed wall time or a mocked SecurityRunner. Process-spawn latency and abnormal uninterruptible OS cleanup are not newly qualified by this slice.

Awaited timeout/overflow kills and joins the direct child. Future drop retains Tokio kill_on_drop behavior; safe Drop cannot await, so only eventual cleanup on a live runtime is qualified, not synchronous cancellation joining or descendant-group cleanup.

No actual Keychain/security-account/provider calls, user settings, Cargo feature changes, central ledger edits, release/tag/publish actions or numerical performance/platform qualification. Earlier release artifacts and limit-audit reports remain historical; root owns the combined fresh candidate validation.
